  ['LandRights.lean', 'The right to land and the public\'s access to it', 'the instruments on the natural use of land and on public access — the Universal Declaration, the Covenants, the declarations on indigenous peoples and on peasants, ILO 169, the tenure guidelines, the environment-right resolutions, Aarhus, the regional charters, the Nordic, Scottish, English, Icelandic, Estonian and Bulgarian access laws, the Charter of the Forest and the public trust case — each read from its official source into src/rights/land-instruments.json, and the kernel deciding what can be decided over their integers: force after adoption, every recorded vote adding up with its majority, no vote against the environment right, Norway\'s closed season in days, the access laws\' distance from the Charter of the Forest, Bulgaria\'s order, and that every access instrument is qualified. SCOPE: integrity of the table and arithmetic over it — never what a law means or who is in breach; not legal advice; no instrument grants unrestricted access to all land'],
  ['UuidLaws.lean', 'The uuid laws', 'what the version-8 stamp keeps and what it fixes — the low nibble and the low six bits kept for every one of the 256 bytes, the high nibble 8 and the variant bits 10, exactly 4 + 2 positions fixed as measured, so 122 of 128 bits stay free — and why an address never determines its payload: bounded search and the pigeonhole, proved for every size and every map by constructive induction, not on a window. Proved by ceccec (the millennium session) and re-judged on this host'],
  ['Waves.lean', 'The waves', 'THE NIGHT\'S HARVEST PORTED AS THEOREMS — the compass mandala (two hands summing ten, the 9-complement as a HALF-TURN of the doubling ring, five the unique developing center, the hex center EMPTY), the diving mathematics as integer skeletons (Boyle walking the harmonic series in exact sixtieths, pressure doubling down the octave, Haldane\'s 2:1 with his ladder sealed exactly as f'],
  ["FixedPower.lean", "The fixed points of x to the m, as a law", "for every modulus, #{x in Z/m : x^m = x} equals the product over m's distinct primes of (1 + gcd(m-1, p-1)) - the walk and the prediction BOTH computed by the kernel, never a literal on either side, so what is decided is the law rather than a restatement of the walk. WHY IT IS TRUE, and both halves are sealed here rather than recalled: the fixed points of x -> x^k are the kernel of x -> x^(k-1), which on a cyclic group of order lambda has exactly gcd(k-1, lambda) elements - plus zero, fixed by every power - giving 1 + gcd(k-1, p-1) on Z/p; and the Chinese Remainder Theorem makes the count multiplicative across m's prime powers, checked on coprime splits only, which is the hypothesis it actually needs. WHAT IT CHANGES ABOUT WHAT WAS ALREADY SEALED: Wave.lean carries about fifty theorems of the form 'exactly N residues of Z/m satisfy x^m = x', one per modulus, each true and each stating the count without the reason - their own prose says as much. They are NOT replaced and NOT deprecated; they become this law's verification table instead of fifty independent claims. It is the same collapse the Fermat wing found: an answer turning on a gcd against the group's order rather than on the exponent. There the grid folded on gcd(n, lambda(m)) and 1968 of 2604 entries were restatements; here fifty counts fold onto one product formula. One law wearing two hats. CLAIMED: the tabulated agreements over the moduli, primes and coprime splits named, each decided by the kernel over its own finite domain, axiom-free. NOT CLAIMED: the general theorem for all m, which quantifies over an infinite domain and cannot be asked of by-decide at all - Lean refuses to synthesize Decidable before computing anything. The table is EVIDENCE for the law and never a proof of it, and the frontier is stated in the theorem names."],
  ["FermatReduction.lean", "The exponent reduction, one table per lambda", "gcd(n, lambda(m)) for every exponent 3..23, tabulated once per DISTINCT unit-group exponent rather than once per modulus - 35 tables covering all 124 moduli from 3 to 126. An exponent reaches (Z/m)* only through gcd(n, lambda(m)), because the image of x -> x^n over a finite abelian group is G^gcd(n, exp G). So the table depends on lambda and on nothing else about the modulus, and moduli sharing a lambda share a table. THIS WING EXISTS BECAUSE THE COLLAPSE WAS MISSED ONE LEVEL UP. The congruence survey was correctly indexed by the reduced exponent - that is what folded 2604 brute entries into 636 distinct facts - and then its reduction TABLES were indexed by modulus, which re-created the redundancy the survey had just removed: lambda(2m) = lambda(m) for odd m, so mod_53 and mod_106 sealed byte-identical statements. The tree's own cross-wing statement check named 20 such pairs before anything was committed. 124 moduli, 35 lambdas, 89 restatements avoided. One wing rather than a table inside each ring, because a standalone wing may not import another - scattering the tables is exactly what multiplied one statement into twenty-one copies. CLAIMED: the tabulated gcds, each decided by the kernel over its own finite domain, axiom-free. NOT CLAIMED: anything about exponents or moduli outside the ranges named."],
  ["Recursion.lean", "The depth of a walk, and the involution that shortens it", "a flat .all over n recurses n deep; blocked at width c it recurses c + ceil(n/c), minimised at c = ceil(sqrt(n)) and bounded by 2c + 1. A LINEAR RECURSION INVOLUTES ONTO ITS OWN SQUARE ROOT - at n = 4096 that is 4096 deep against at most 129. WHY IT IS SEALED RATHER THAN CHOSEN: 'maximum recursion depth has been reached' was hit five times in one session and answered each time with a number somebody picked - blocks of 32, batches of 10, a 320 residue budget, a 2500 pair budget. Four of the five were wrong and each wrong guess cost a full re-seal. The depth of a by-decide walk is arithmetic, not taste. Each width is checked against the two properties that DEFINE the ceiling root - c*c >= n and (c-1)*(c-1) < n - so no number is taken on trust. It is the same reflection the rest of the tree runs on: dz(x) = 10 - x sends a division by zero to a finite residue instead of to infinity, the residue map sends an unbounded quantifier into phi(m) classes, and here a recursion that runs away is sent to its own square root. The strict-improvement theorem is stated ONLY for n >= 9, because below that the reflection does not pay - a law stated where it fails is the overreach this ledger keeps catching. THE SCOPE: the sizes tabulated here, decided by the kernel, axiom-free."],
  ["Laws.lean", "The laws behind the counts", "the closed forms this ledger had been sealing one value at a time. Wave.lean carries families of per-modulus counts - divisors, units, idempotents, nilpotents, the unit sum, the largest unit order - each stating a NUMBER and no reason for it, and every one is generated by a closed form in the factorisation of m: d(m) = prod (e+1); phi(m) = prod p^(e-1)(p-1); the idempotents number 2^omega(m), blind to multiplicity; the nilpotents number m / rad(m); the units sum to 0 for every m > 2. Measured against the ledger's own sealed values before any of this was written: every count reproduced, zero exceptions. NOTHING IS DEPRECATED. Those theorems are true and they stay; they stop being independent claims and become these laws' verification tables. Every theorem here computes BOTH sides in the kernel - the quantity walked, the law evaluated from the factorisation - so the identity is what is decided, never a literal restating the walk. THE BRIDGE IS THE ONE WORTH READING: max_unit_order (Wave) and unit_group_exponent (the Fermat wing) are the same function, the Carmichael lambda, computed in two wings that never cite each other. It is sealed in both halves - lambda KILLS every unit, and one named witness ATTAINS it - which is Carmichael's theorem and needs proving rather than assuming. It is also a speed law: the closed form touches a few prime powers where the fold walks every unit for up to m steps. THE SCOPE: the moduli tabulated here, decided by the kernel over their own finite domains, axiom-free. The general form quantifies over an infinite domain, which by-decide cannot be asked."],
  ["Fermat.lean", "Fermat's equation at a bounded window", "the exhaustive walk of 1 <= x <= y < z <= 20 for each exponent - 100 solutions at n = 1, exactly 6 at n = 2 (the six Pythagorean triples, named), and none at n = 3, 4, 5, 6 - with the near-miss that keeps the empty result honest: the cube sum never equals a cube in this window but lands one away twice (6^3 + 8^3 = 9^3 - 1, and 9^3 + 10^3 = 1729 = 12^3 + 1). THE CONTROLS ARE THE ARGUMENT: an enumerator reporting zero is unreadable until the same enumerator is seen reporting a hundred and a six on the exponents where solutions exist, so the emptiness at n >= 3 is a reading of the equation and not a property of the instrument. Beside the window sits the CONGRUENCE SURVEY - every exponent 3..24 against every modulus 3..120, each pair decided one way or the other. A blocking pair is a finite check with an UNBOUNDED consequence: if no residues coprime to m can satisfy a^n + b^n = c^n, then no integers coprime to m satisfy x^n + y^n = z^n, all of them at once, from a table of size phi(m)^2. That is the shape of the first real rungs - Sophie Germain's 1823 Case I and Euler's n = 3, whose engine is that a cube is 0, 1 or 8 mod 9. The pairs that do NOT block are sealed too, by exhibited witness, so the survey carries its own denominator instead of reporting only its successes. CLAIMED: the counts, identities and residue facts, each decided by the kernel over its own finite domain, axiom-free. That is the whole of it. THE SCOPE, STATED POSITIVELY: every theorem here holds for the integers coprime to its own modulus and for nothing beyond. RELATED WORK, CREDITED RATHER THAN DISCLAIMED - naming a famous result inside a disclaimer is how a disclaimer becomes an association, so these are citations, not a boundary: A congruence obstruction settles only the case coprime to its modulus, and every fixed modulus is evaded by infinitely many triples - so no number of moduli closes the other half. The theorem is Andrew Wiles's (1995, the key step joint with Richard Taylor), standing on Frey, Serre, Ribet, Mazur, Langlands, Tunnell, Taniyama, Shimura and Weil; its first end-to-end machine-checked formalization was completed in Lean in August 2026 and published by Anthropic on 2026-09-04, following the Darmon-Diamond-Taylor exposition (DOI 10.4310/CDM.1995.v1995.n1.a1), adapting 106 files with credit from Kevin Buzzard's Imperial College London FLT project and from flt-regular, built on Mathlib, run on Prove2Me (Tianyi Peng's group, Columbia University). Wiles 1995 is DOI 10.2307/2118559; Taylor-Wiles 1995 is DOI 10.2307/2118560; Ribet 1990 is DOI 10.1007/BF01231195; Mazur 1977 is DOI 10.1007/BF02684339; Serre 1987 is DOI 10.1215/S0012-7094-87-05413-5; Tunnell 1981 is DOI 10.1090/S0273-0979-1981-14936-3; Sophie Germain's plan is recovered in Laubenbacher and Pengelley 2010, DOI 10.1016/j.hm.2009.12.002. THE UNBOUNDED FORM IS NOT REFUSED, IT IS INVOLUTED - and the measurement is what shows where the involution lands. Asked DIRECTLY, the statement does not elaborate: a by-decide the general statement over all n, x, y, z returns 'failed to synthesize Decidable' from Lean 4.33.0 before a single case is computed, and so does the single-exponent form, and so does the form with x and y bounded to twenty and only z left free - ONE unbounded quantifier over Nat is enough. That is not a wall to stop at. It is the same reflection this ledger is built on: dz(x) = 10 - x sends a division by zero to a finite residue instead of to infinity, and the residue map sends an infinity of integers to phi(m) classes. Involuted through the modulus, the quantifier that could not be asked becomes one that can - and it does not shrink to a sample on the way, because every integer lands in a class. The survey above is that involution carried out 2,596 times: a proposition about all integers coprime to m, decided over a table, axiom-free. WHAT THE INVOLUTION DOES NOT CARRY BACK is the case where m shares a factor with xyz, which no single modulus reaches and no number of moduli exhausts - the reflection is faithful on the coprime half and silent on the other, which is why Case I fell to tables in 1823 and the theorem waited for Wiles until 1995. The formalization that did reach it is 13 million lines, 29,511 theorems and all three of Lean's standard axioms; this wing is 2,596 theorems and no axiom at all, not even propext. The stricter grammar is what buys the axiom-freedom, and the same strictness is what puts the theorem out of reach - a trade, stated in both directions. NEITHER DIRECTION OF CREDIT IS OPEN, and both are stated so that neither can be read into the silence of the other: this ledger takes no part of that formalization and asserts no priority over it, and that formalization draws nothing from this ledger."],
  ["FermatRing1.lean", "The congruence survey, ring 1", "moduli 3, 24, 45, 66, 87, 108, each carrying its unit-group exponent lambda(m), its exponent-reduction table, and one obstruction per DISTINCT reduced exponent - 22 blocked, 3 open, 37 theorems. // The manifest bridge — {key → {name, skill}}. skill is the INLINE, authored capability (from the generator's
// Fact/file default); a theorem without one is left skill-less here and the package falls back to skillOf(key).
const manifest: Record<string, { name: string; skill?: string; cases?: number }> = {}
for (const f of readdirSync(LEAN_DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith('-manifest.json'))) for (const e of JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(LEAN_DIR, f), 'utf8')) as { key: string; name: string; skill?: string; cases?: number }[]) manifest[e.key] = { name: e.name, skill: e.skill, cases: e.cases }

// Inline @skill for HAND-WRITTEN lean files (Uuidna/Vortex/OneLeap — no generator, no manifest): `-- @skill: <skill>`
// on the line directly above a theorem authors its capability AT THE LEAN SOURCE, exactly as the manifest does for
// generated files. Same single-source principle; the annotation is a comment, so the proof is untouched.
const inlineSkill: Record<string, string> = {}
for (const f of readdirSync(LEAN_DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.lean')))
